golden_tests.verdict: Execution engine directionally CORRECT. Defects are in masking and accounting, not in trade direction.

signal_polarity.test: EURUSD, S3 momentum signal, h=30min, buggy mask
signal_polarity.explanation: Flipping signal polarity does NOT transform negative gross to positive. Gross remains negative (-2611) when flipped. This rules out a simple sign inversion. The signal is genuinely anti-predictive (or has no predictive power and the negative gross is from adverse execution timing).
signal_polarity.conclusion: Even at mid-price (removing spread effect), P&L is negative. Signal has negative or zero predictive power at 30-min horizon.

pair_orientation.explanation: All 13 pairs use the same execution formula: long=(bid_exit-ask_entry)/ask_entry, short=(bid_entry-ask_exit)/bid_entry. This is correct regardless of quote orientation (USD-quoted, JPY-quoted, etc.) because it operates on actual bid/ask prices, not on a normalized return. The golden tests (A-C) confirm correct directional behavior.

date_role_decomposition.finding: 2009-2013 (unauthorized) contributes 60% of total loss. 2014-2017 (authorized) still shows negative gross in all periods. The signal is anti-predictive in ALL periods, not just the unauthorized ones.
date_role_decomposition.label: POST_OUTCOME_DESCRIPTIVE_ONLY

s2_leakage.impact: The full-sample median is 28.8% LOWER than the early-period median. This means the buggy threshold classifies more bars as 'high vol' (conf=1.0) than a causal threshold would. Effect: slightly more aggressive signals in early periods. Direction of bias: amplifies signal magnitude, does not change sign.
s2_leakage.severity: MODERATE (does not change sign of results, only magnitude)

turnover_audit.finding: All S1-S5 hit exactly 3.0 trades/instrument-day (the cap). S7 = 0 trades.
turnover_audit.explanation: The signals are continuous (non-zero at nearly every bar). With 288 five-min bars per day and signals non-zero at >90% of bars, the 3-trade cap is reached within the first 3 eligible bars of each day. This is NOT a bug - it is the expected behavior when signals are always active. The cap is working correctly.

spread_double_counting.mechanism: gross = (bid_exit - ask_entry)/ask_entry already includes spread crossing. Then net = gross - spread_c - comm subtracts spread AGAIN.
spread_double_counting.conclusion: Double-counting makes net ~34% more negative. However, even the corrected net (gross - comm) is still negative, and the mid-price P&L is also negative. The signal is genuinely anti-predictive.

statistics_status.note: Statistics cannot be computed without the full 13-instrument corrected run completing. However, the qualitative conclusion (all negative) does not depend on multiplicity correction - if ALL candidates are negative, no multiple testing adjustment can make them positive.

classification_reasoning.engineering_bugs_explain: Spread double-counting (34% excess loss) and date filter (60% of loss from unauthorized period) are real engineering defects that make results more negative than they should be.
classification_reasoning.signal_failure_explains: Even after removing both engineering bugs, the mid-price P&L is still negative (-1512 bps for EURUSD). Flipping polarity does not help. The signal is genuinely anti-predictive at 30-min FX horizons. This is a SIGNAL FAILURE.
classification_reasoning.conclusion: Both matter. Engineering bugs amplify the loss, but the core issue is that momentum/trend signals at 15m-4h horizons in FX have negative or zero predictive power. The corrected result would still be negative.
